title: Playing in Tom Albert's string band
summary: Happy played in Tom Albert's string band, who drank his own whiskey, with banjo, clarinet by John Handy and a bass player named Jake.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section's changing role

blocks.x: He's got the old band there.
That's a wartime. He look good too. Yeah, we ought to see him again.
Yeah, I'm just saying I didn't think I had the band.
You say you played with him though, huh? Yeah.
You played in a string band?
We better put it on here. This is Happy Goldstone, Reel 3. What was it? April the 10th, 1962.
And we better put that we were talking about Tom Albert because I don't think that got on the tape.
So he had a string band and he played in the Eureka too, huh? Yeah.

We, Tom Albert, we played string band. He used to bring his own whiskey. He didn't wait for the people to give him whiskey. Because sometimes we played plays with the Annali liquor. Tom would get his bottle and go by the band and drink it.
You played with his string band you say? I played with his string band. And who was in the band with him?
Which Barnes? Frank Warp player. Jules. Jules Barnes. Charlie Moore.
Which instrument did he play then? Banjo or guitar or what? He played banjo. Banjo at that time. Mm-hmm. Have a clarinet player? Saxophone player? No, they had a clarinet. Handy. Yeah.

A handy from downtown. John Handy, sure. John Handy, sure. John Handy, yeah. I must have had a bass player or a piano player. Yeah, they had a bass player, I just remember. Jake. Jake, huh? Yeah, probably they called Jake. Mm-hmm.
